s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with pleuritic and diaphoretic characteristics, associated with elevated troponin and inflammatory markers, in a young adult with recent onset of ulcerative colitis
salient_findings: Pleuritic pain worsened by sitting forward
Extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
key_facts: 2-day history of intermittent, sharp, central chest pain
Pain is pleuritic and worsens when sitting forward
Diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 3 weeks prior to admission
No family history of cardiovascular disease
ECG shows sinus rhythm with benign early repolarization
Negative serum viral and autoantibody screens
Transthoracic echocardiography shows borderline low systolic function
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging shows extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on CMR, and borderline low systolic function

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease-associated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and cardiac involvement suggested by elevated troponin and abnormal CMR findings

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and diaphoretic chest pain, although young age and absence of family history of cardiovascular disease make this less likely

shortlist.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Young adult with chest pain and elevated troponin, although less common than other causes

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patchy late gadolinium enhancement on CMR and elevated inflammatory markers, although less common than myocarditis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sharp, central chest pain, elevated high-sensitivity troponin T, and extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, along with elevated C-reactive protein, is most consistent with myocarditis, especially given the lack of evidence for coronary artery disease or other cardiomyopathies.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease-associated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has ulcerative colitis, the temporal relationship and the specific cardiac findings are more suggestive of myocarditis than a cardiomyopathy directly associated with his bowel disease.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's age, lack of risk factors for atherosclerosis, and the pattern of cardiac enzyme elevation and imaging findings make acute coronary syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of coronary artery dissection provided in the case, and the imaging findings are more consistent with myocardial inflammation than with a dissection.

rejected.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While cardiac sarcoidosis can present with similar imaging findings, the acute presentation and lack of other systemic symptoms or findings suggestive of sarcoidosis make this diagnosis less likely in this case.
